'''John Fauvel''' (21 July 1947 – 12 May 2001) was a British mathematician and historian of mathematics.<ref name="Guardian">{{cite news| first=Jeremy | last=Gray | author-link=Jeremy Gray (mathematician) | title=John Fauvel – Chronicler of the history of mathematics | newspaper=[[The Guardian]] | date=22 June 2001 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2001/jun/22/guardianobituaries.obituaries }}</ref><ref name="LMS">{{cite journal| first=J. J. | last=Gray | author-link=Jeremy Gray (mathematician) | title=Obituary: John Grant Fauvel (1947–2001) | journal=[[Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]] | volume=35 | number=4 | date=July 2003 | pages=565–569 | doi=10.1112/S0024609302001674 | publisher=[[London Mathematical Society]] | doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Education==
Fauvel was from [[Scotland]], where his father was a [[Principal (education)|principal]].
[[Ian Blair]] was a cousin.

John attended [[Trinity College, Glenalmond]]. He then studied mathematics at the [[University of Essex]], where he graduated in 1970, and at the [[University of Warwick]], where he obtained his master's degree in 1973. In 1977, he obtained his [[Master of Philosophy|MPhil]] from the University of Warwick under the supervision of David Orme Tall, with a thesis entitled ''Fuzzy Theory''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|85554}}</ref>

==Career==
From 1974, Fauvel worked at the [[Open University]]. From 1991 to 1994, he was President of the [[British Society for the History of Mathematics]] and he also edited its newsletter. From 1992 to 1996, he directed an international study group on the relations between history and mathematics pedagogy, which is affiliated with the [[International Commission for Mathematical Education]] (ICMI), and in 2000 he co-directed a major study of ICMI. In 1998, he was invited lecturer by the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]].<ref name="Guardian" /> Fauvel was a visiting scholar in the Mathematics Department at [[Colorado College]] on several occasions, including one on a [[Fulbright Fellowship]] during the Winter and Spring of 1999.

Fauvel died on 12 May 2001 of complications from liver disease.<ref name="Guardian" />
